mercury.credit: NASA / Johns Hopkins APL / Carnegie Institution of Washington; MESSENGER MDIS MD3 colour mosaic via USGS Astrogeology
mercury.licence: Public domain (NASA mission data, distributed by USGS)
mercury.shows: false colour: MDIS 1000 / 750 / 430 nm filters in R / G / B, not what the eye would see
mercury.projection: simple cylindrical (equirectangular), latitude +90 at the top edge, -90 at the bottom
mercury.notes: A few rows at each pole have no data and are black.

venus.credit: NASA / JPL; Magellan C3-MDIR radar mosaic coloured by altimetry, via USGS Astrogeology
venus.licence: Public domain (NASA mission data, distributed by USGS)
venus.shows: radar: Magellan SAR backscatter, colour codes elevation (blue low, red high); the surface under the clouds, not the visible planet
venus.projection: simple cylindrical (equirectangular), latitude +90 at the top edge, -90 at the bottom

earth.credit: NASA Earth Observatory / NASA Scientific Visualization Studio; Blue Marble: Next Generation (Terra MODIS), July 2004
earth.shows: true colour, cloud-free monthly composite with shaded topography
earth.projection: simple cylindrical (equirectangular), latitude +90 at the top edge, -90 at the bottom

moon.credit: NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio; CGI Moon Kit from LRO LROC WAC data
moon.shows: near true colour, LROC WAC mosaic with the poles filled
moon.projection: simple cylindrical (equirectangular), latitude +90 at the top edge, -90 at the bottom

mars.credit: NASA / USGS / NASA Ames; Viking Orbiter colour mosaic over MDIM 2.1
mars.shows: approximate true colour, Viking colour blended over the MDIM 2.1 mosaic
mars.projection: simple cylindrical (equirectangular), latitude +90 at the top edge, -90 at the bottom

jupiter.credit: NASA / JPL / Space Science Institute; Cassini ISS, PIA07782, December 2000
jupiter.shows: near true colour, built from 750 nm and 451 nm frames
jupiter.projection: simple cylindrical (equirectangular), latitude +90 at the top edge, -90 at the bottom
jupiter.notes: Grid version labels System III west longitude 180 (left) .. 0 (centre) .. 180 (right), i.e. east longitude increases to the right. The source is 3601x1801 with a repeated edge column and row, cropped to 3600x1800 before resampling.

skipped.saturn: No global cylindrical colour map of Saturn's cloud tops is published on NASA / JPL / USGS domains; Cassini maps there cover only the moons and rings.
skipped.uranus: Voyager 2 saw an almost featureless disc; no global map exists from NASA sources.
skipped.neptune: Voyager 2 imaged only part of the planet during one flyby; no global map exists from NASA sources.
